_note: Written by the cloud worker, NOT by exist.py. exist.py raised before writing its own result JSON because drat-trim's first pass hit drat-trim's internal 40000 s limit and chirosat.run_drat_trim treats any non-VERIFIED output as a rejection. The check was then rerun by hand against the same proof file with -t 400000 and returned s VERIFIED. Timings marked derived come from file mtimes and heartbeat lines, not from exist.py's perf_counter fields.
solver: cadical 1.7.3 (Debian package /usr/bin/cadical; --version prints 1.7.3, package version 1.7.4-1), single threaded, nice -n 5
checker: drat-trim built from github.com/marijnheule/drat-trim at HEAD, cloned 2026-09-04

drat_trim_attempt_1.note: Not a rejection. drat-trim exhausted its built-in limit (TIMEOUT 40000, drat-trim.c:29) during backward checking and exits 0 in that case, which is why the exit code was 0 while stdout said TIMEOUT. exist.py's --timeout 36000 is passed only to the cadical subprocess and never reached drat-trim.

drat_trim_attempt_2.note: Run against the same proof file, unmodified: its mtime (2026-09-05T06:18:45Z) predates both the sha256 above (taken 17:26Z) and this check, so the bytes hashed are the bytes verified. The 165 'backward mode ignores deletion of (pseudo) unit clause' warnings are drat-trim declining to honour deletions of unit clauses in backward mode; it therefore keeps more clauses live than the proof asks it to, which makes the check stricter, not weaker.

lost_run.note: A first launch of the same job at 2026-09-04T23:54:34Z was killed at 2026-09-05T01:01:07Z (about 66 minutes in) when the microVM was suspended during a session idle window and rebooted at 01:15:49Z. No result; its 1.86 GB partial proof was discarded and the job restarted from scratch at 01:18:36Z. Thereafter the session was held in foreground waits so the VM was never idle.

smoke_test.note: Both digests match the reference run recorded in REPORT-EXIST.md Section 4 exactly, so this worker reproduces the reference toolchain bit for bit.

what_this_establishes: Cube 3 of the (15,32) existence SAT is UNSAT with a DRAT proof verified by drat-trim. By Lemma 7 of REPORT-EXIST.md the four cubes partition every row-1 configuration (orbit sizes 120+1440+640+3840 = 6040 = the enumerated total), so this closes one of the four. It does NOT by itself settle t3(15): cubes 0, 1 and 2 are separate jobs and all four must be UNSAT before the argument of REPORT-EXIST.md concludes that no rank-3 chirotope on 15 elements has a PTS(15,32) as its zero set, and hence that t3(15) = 31.
reproducing: The proof is not committed (8.98 GB). Regenerate with the command above using cadical 1.7.3; the CNF is deterministic and should match cnf_sha256. The proof is solver-run dependent and need not match proof_sha256 byte for byte; any DRAT proof cadical emits for this CNF should verify.
recommendation_for_the_other_cubes: Pass -t explicitly to drat-trim, or raise TIMEOUT in drat-trim.c. On this hardware cube 3 needed 45332 s of checking against 18004 s of solving, a ratio of about 2.5, so the default 40000 s limit will silently truncate any cube of comparable size and surface as a spurious 'proof rejected'.
